channel.title: Muhammad Jahanzaib Awan — Writing
channel.description: Short technical posts on machine learning, evaluation and data science.

item.title: Machine Learning Definitions Compared: The Quiet Disagreements
item.description: Textbooks all quote similar definitions of machine learning, but look closely and they disagree on what counts as learning, generalisation, and experience.

item.title: What Genetic Perturbation Models Teach Us About Deep Learning
item.description: Models that predict cellular response to gene perturbations look impressive until you check the splits. The lessons generalise far beyond biology.

item.title: Context Engineering Versus Prompt Engineering: What Changed
item.description: Prompt wording still matters, but the real leverage moved to what you retrieve, structure, and feed a model before it answers.

item.title: Choosing a First NLP Project That Actually Teaches You Something
item.description: Skip the chatbot clone. A simple classifier, built with care, teaches tokenisation, embeddings, and evaluation far better.

item.title: What a Fine-Tuning Run Actually Costs
item.description: GPU hours are the visible cost of fine-tuning. Data curation and honest evaluation are the invisible costs that decide whether the run was worth it.

item.title: Evaluating a Model Against Its Own Baseline, Not Just the Leaderboard
item.description: Beating the leaderboard means little if your model cannot beat a trivial baseline built from its own inputs. Here is why that comparison matters.

item.title: Why Computer Vision and ML Engineers Read Papers Differently
item.description: Computer vision and general ML engineers scan the same paper for different red flags, shaped by different failure modes they have each been burned by.

item.title: A Worked Example of Overfitting to the Leaderboard
item.description: Checking the leaderboard too often quietly turns your test set into training data. Here is a worked example showing exactly how.

item.title: The Vocabulary Trap in ML Job Adverts
item.description: ML job titles like NLP Engineer, CV Engineer, and MLOps Engineer look distinct on paper, but the actual day-to-day skills overlap heavily once you look past the buzzwords.

item.title: Building a Threat-Aware Evaluation Harness, Sensibly
item.description: Most evaluation harnesses test for competence, not failure. Borrowing a few habits from red-team thinking fixes that, without needing a security team.

item.title: Model Evaluation as a Discipline: Metric Versus Decision
item.description: Accuracy is a number. Deployment is a decision. This post explains the discipline that separates the two, with a worked example.

item.title: Held-Out Evaluation for Recommenders: When Offline Lies
item.description: High offline NDCG does not guarantee happy users. A walk through why held-out splits mislead recommender evaluation and how to close the gap.

item.title: Computer Vision Book or Course: What Each One Teaches
item.description: A book gives you the mathematics and the why; a course gives you the workflow and the muscle memory. Most learners need both, in the right order.

item.title: Data Annotation Quality: Your Labels Are the Real Model
item.description: Model architecture gets the glory, but in NLP the annotation guidelines and inter-annotator agreement quietly decide your ceiling. Here is why that ceiling is usually lower than you think.

item.title: What Counts as an NLP Practitioner Before Deep Learning
item.description: Deep learning did not invent NLP; it rebranded a field that already had decades of rigorous, rule-based practice worth remembering.

item.title: Full Fine-Tuning vs PEFT: A Decision Framework, Not a Trend
item.description: LoRA and its cousins are useful, not magic. Here is how to actually decide when full fine-tuning still earns its cost.

item.title: Fine-Tuning as a Word: What Physics Lent Machine Learning
item.description: Machine learning didn't invent fine-tuning. It borrowed a loaded term from physics and cosmology, and the borrowing changes how we should think about it.

item.title: Curriculum Learning: Ordering Training Data on Purpose
item.description: Most training pipelines shuffle data and hope. Curriculum learning asks what happens if you don't, and the answer is more nuanced than 'easy first, hard later'.

item.title: Explaining a Model's Decision When Nobody Trusts the p-value
item.description: When a p-value fails to persuade, swap it for concrete numbers on money, customers, and risk. Here is how I do that in practice.

item.title: Data Contracts for ML Pipelines: Catching Schema Drift Early
item.description: Schema drift breaks models silently. Data contracts catch it at the source, before it poisons training data or corrupts predictions in production.
